stem:
Pooja stirs kitchen samples into separate glasses of water and waits until the water settles.

Which statement correctly classifies solubility?

options.text: Sugar that disappears completely is soluble; sand that remains at the bottom is insoluble.
Sugar that disappears completely is insoluble; sand that remains undissolved is soluble.
Cooking oil cannot be called soluble or insoluble because solubility applies only to solids.
Any powder that makes the water look cloudy must be more soluble than clear sugar water.

teacher.key_rationale: Complete dissolution means soluble; undissolved material means insoluble. Reversing those labels is wrong, and solubility is not limited to solids alone.
